claims.statement: Open SWE persists one-shot and cron work in a PostgreSQL-backed job queue whose jobs carry a kind, payload, due time, optional cron/timezone, replacement key, metadata, attempts, and a claim token; handlers are registered on a shared worker and the application starts and stops that worker in its lifespan.
A keyed schedule is an upsert that replaces the existing job and clears its lease and attempts; jobs can be cancelled by ID, key, or metadata.

All replicas may poll, but due jobs are claimed transactionally with SKIP LOCKED and a 30-minute lease; the worker limits concurrent work to 20, renews claims every 10 seconds, cancels work when cancellation is observed, and lets interrupted shutdown work be reclaimed after its lease expires.

Successful one-shot jobs are deleted and successful cron jobs advance to their next fire; failed one-shots retry with exponential 30-second-to-one-hour backoff for fewer than five attempts, while failed cron occurrences advance directly to the next fire.

Startup migrates supported non-thread-bound Agent Server crons to queue jobs under a distributed claim, updates each durable owner, deletes migrated legacy crons, and leaves a cron in place when adoption fails; it also ensures the per-minute thread-status reconciliation job.
Schedule dashboard endpoints list schedules for sessions and require audited admin access for create, update, manual trigger, and delete operations.

Automation schedules persist a prompt, explicit workspace, model/effort, enabled and admin-thread settings, and typed cron, GitHub, Slack, or Linear triggers; cron syntax is normalized to five fields, and only schedule triggers create keyed agent_schedule cron jobs.

Schedule creation validates workspace and integration access, and admin-thread automations are restricted to administrators and refused for public GitHub-event repositories because public event content is untrusted.

Each scheduled automation fire is deduplicated for two days by a claim keyed with the queue job ID and due time before launch; its launcher reloads the schedule and trigger, cleans orphan timers where applicable, and returns a status rather than launching when the owner, trigger, workspace, or repository is no longer valid.

A successful automation launch creates a fresh thread and durable agent run whose configuration identifies schedule source, schedule ID, selected workspace/environment, invocation ID, and schedule system sender.

The schedule_thread_wakeup tool accepts delays from one minute through 24 hours, rounds fire time to a UTC minute, persists a one-shot wakeup payload with context and a 90-second expiry, and limits a thread to ten wakeups between human messages using metadata that resets for a new human-message generation.

A due thread wakeup is dropped if expired; otherwise it creates an enqueued agent run with the completion webhook. Wakeup handler failures are logged without queue retry to avoid duplicate runs when the server may have started one before the client error.

Baby-sit watches are persisted on pull-request task state, are owned by the initiating task coordinator, run through a keyed ten-minute queue job, and reject a watch for the same PR from another task.

Baby-sit polling and CI webhooks serialize evaluation with a five-minute event-claim lock; evaluation resets retry/deduplication state for a new head, waits for required checks, dispatches thread handoffs for success or failures, deduplicates a failure by head and retry count, caps flaky reruns at three per head, and eventually stops after three evaluation errors.

Background command completion is reconciled either by authenticated sandbox callback or by a keyed one-minute per-thread polling job; reconciliation validates ownership, tracks running task IDs, claims terminal notifications in the sandbox, dispatches completion to the owning thread with enqueue semantics, marks successful delivery done, and releases the claim after failure for a later retry.

Workspace refreshes use a keyed daily cron staggered between 03:00 and 05:59 UTC or one-shot jobs; a refresh in progress for three hours is considered stale, and reconciliation includes a per-minute busy-thread status repair plus a sweep that interrupts pending runs older than 30 minutes so lost completion webhooks do not leave threads busy forever.

Focused tests verify baby-sit dispatch deduplication, concurrency, green and terminal thread handoff, retry ownership/budgets, and wakeup delay bounds, context, budget generations, cancellation, cleanup, and expiry behavior.
